chain.claim: A full verification, or a requested scope containing 0 registered SPEC records, must yield spec_coverage = MISSING and can never yield PASS (fail-closed on the empty set).
chain.normative_source: Verified verbatim in the canonical docs. 基本仕様 v0.1 §7.4 (line 419): 「完全検証scopeに登録Specificationが0件の場合も`spec_coverage = MISSING`とし、空集合をPASSにしない。」 and §7.4 line 424: 「有効な監査が`COMPLETE`のときだけ`spec_coverage = PASS`」. 別紙C 受入仕様 §18.3.5 (lines 157-158): 「`spec_coverage`は登録Specificationの要求事項がactive REQへ完全に取り込まれたことを有効なspec-coverage監査で確認した場合だけPASSとする。active REQの存在だけ、またはREQ → VO対応の存在だけでPASSにしない。」 / 「登録Specificationが0件の完全検証を`spec_coverage = MISSING`とし、空集合をPASSにしない。」 詳細設計 v0.1 line 1333 repeats the SPEC-bound rule (source current + >=1 active REQ + valid spec-coverage audit bound to the SPEC subject and the complete corresponding REQ set).
chain.mechanism: spec_coverage is designed as a SPEC-rooted item: its subject is the registered Specification source content hash plus the complete set of active REQs referencing that SPEC, evaluated through a `spec-coverage` semantic audit record (基本仕様 §7.4, §8; 別紙C §18.3.4). With zero SPEC subjects there is nothing to bind an audit to, so the fail-closed degenerate value is MISSING, never a vacuous PASS.
chain.condition: A project whose .verify/spec/ contains 0 SPEC records, with at least one REQ record that has spec_refs: [] and at least one VO linking that REQ. Reachable because `vtest req add` without --spec stores spec_refs: [] (crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs, spec_refs_from_args) and `vtest vo add --req REQ-A` links the REQ; no command or gate requires a SPEC record to exist before verify runs.
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:546-582 — the "spec_coverage" arm of evaluate_item(). It builds `reqs` from selection.req_ids and `vos` from selection.vo_ids, computes `missing` = REQs with no linked VO, and returns CheckValue::Pass with basis "every selected REQ has at least one linked VO" whenever `!reqs.is_empty() && missing.is_empty()`. No SPEC record, SPEC dir, spec_refs field, or spec-coverage audit record is read anywhere on this path; the crate's only spec reads are audit-subject reads at lines 1538/1583-1584 (impl-consistency subject building). Full-scope selection sets req_ids to every REQ record (ScopeSelection, crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:~180-190). The verify tree attaches spec_coverage to req nodes (build_req_node, line 416/444); there is no SPEC root node at all.
chain.expected: With 0 registered SPECs, both `vtest verify` (full 12 items) and `vtest verify --items spec_coverage` must report spec_coverage = MISSING, and the limited scope must not be OK.
chain.actual: Reproduced on the prebuilt binary in an isolated temp project: `vtest verify --items spec_coverage` reports spec_coverage = PASS with basis "every selected REQ has at least one linked VO", overall Result: PASS, exit 0, while `vtest spec list` returns {"items":[]}. Full `vtest verify` also reports spec_coverage = PASS (overall MISSING only because test_existence is MISSING for the uncovered VO).
chain.negation: Decisive at system level, not a local omission. (a) The forbidden value is produced by the item itself, in both full scope and item scope, with the exact basis the spec explicitly outlaws (「REQ → VO対応の存在だけでPASSにしない」). (b) No other gate rescues it: with 0 SPECs the request scope `--items spec_coverage` aggregated to overall PASS with exit 0, so the empty-SPEC set is promoted to a green result end-to-end; the fold in node_with_children/combine_values only ever sees the PASS value. (c) The triggering state is trivially reachable through supported CLI commands — nothing in init/req add/vo add/verify requires a SPEC record, and there is no SPEC node in the verification tree that could carry a MISSING. (d) The counter-reading that this is merely 'not yet implemented' (実装スケジュール M6 lists 「active REQの存在だけで`spec_coverage`をPASSにせず」 as a gate condition, M6 marked REVALIDATION_REQUIRED) does not negate the contradiction: the schedule states it as a required gate, not as a permitted staged exemption, and the shipped binary currently emits the forbidden PASS.

chain.claim: Non-PASS test_traceability lists each unregistered or mis-corresponding test with adapter ID, source location, diagnostic code and verdict, identically in text and JSON reports.
chain.normative_source: 别纸A (詳細設計 別紙A インターフェース仕様 v0.1) §12.2 `vtest verify`, lines 225-227, verbatim: 「`test_traceability`はrepository-level項目であり、要求された場合はSPEC / REQ / VO / TESTのentity scopeにかかわらず全Discovered Testを評価する。非PASS時は、未登録または不正対応の各Testについてadapter ID、source location、diagnostic code、判定値をProject checks配下に表示する。JSONでも同じ根拠一覧を返す。」 Supported by 別紙C §18.3.5 (「reportはSPEC → REQ → VO → Testの構造と、各非PASSの根拠をtext / JSONで返す」) and 要件定義 §23 (未登録Testを検証済みとして扱わない / 可視化). The doc really states it — I read the sections directly, not via the candidate.
chain.mechanism: scan adapters emit W-SCAN-101 / E-SCAN-007 (ManagedTestLink::Missing) and E-SCAN-002 / E-SCAN-003 (mis-correspondence) with a Diagnostic carrying code + SourceLocation{adapter, path, locator, byte_range}. vtest-verify folds those diagnostics into ReportItem{item, value, basis} for `test_traceability`; the CLI renders the same VerificationResult in text and JSON, so the per-test evidence must survive into both renderings.
chain.condition: A project containing one `#[test]` function with no `@vtest` annotation (tests/unregistered.rs) alongside one correctly registered Test. This yields W-SCAN-101 -> test_traceability = MISSING -> non-PASS report, which is exactly the state 別紙A §12.2 governs.
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:659-677 `evaluate_test_traceability` -> basis built as `diagnostic.message.clone()` only (code, SourceLocation and adapter discarded); crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:51-55 `ReportItem{item, value, basis: Vec<String>}`; crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:2454-2607 `run_verify` -> `emit(format, quiet, JsonEnvelope::new(ok, to_value(&result), diagnostics))`; crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:3854-3934 `emit_text` (renders tree or items as item+value, never `basis`; prints diagnostics as `severity code: message`, dropping `location`) and 3937-3959 `print_text_tree_node` (item+value only); crates/vtest-model/src/lib.rs:310-316 `SourceLocation{adapter, path, locator, byte_range}` and 670-679 `Diagnostic{code, severity, message, candidates, location}` — the adapter/location data exists in the model and is serialized only on the JSON path.
chain.expected: For test_traceability = MISSING, both the text report and the JSON report list the offending test with (a) adapter ID `rust-cargo`, (b) source location `tests/unregistered.rs::unregistered_fixture_test`, (c) diagnostic code `W-SCAN-101`, (d) verdict MISSING — the same 根拠一覧 in both formats, shown under the project-level check.
chain.actual: Observed on the isolated temp project. TEXT (`verify --items test_traceability --format text`): the `test_traceability` item line is not printed at all (emit_text prints `tree` when present and the tree carries only VO/Test nodes, so the project-level `items` array is never rendered); no `Project checks` section exists in the CLI at all (grep for the literal finds nothing); `basis` is never printed by either emit_text or print_text_tree_node; the only trace is `Result: MISSING` plus one diagnostic line `warning W-SCAN-101: test function `unregistered_fixture_test` has no @vtest annotation` — carrying code and message but no adapter ID, no source location, and no verdict. JSON (`--format json`): the `test_traceability` item appears with `"value": "MISSING"` and `"basis": ["test function `unregistered_fixture_test` has no @vtest annotation"]` — message only, no adapter/location/code — while the separate `diagnostics` array carries the full `location` object including `"adapter": "rust-cargo"`, `"path": "tests/unregistered.rs"`, `"locator": "unregistered_fixture_test"`. (Note: the candidate's assertion that the W-SCAN-101 message is 'only the function name' is wrong — the message is the full sentence above; I report what I observed, not the candidate's wording.)
chain.negation: System-level, not a local omission. The state is reachable and terminal: verify ran to completion, produced the non-PASS report and exit 1; no earlier gate rejects it — the report IS the output, and `vtest report` shares the identical `run_verify`/`emit_text` path, so there is no alternative rendering that supplies the missing facts. Both prongs of the claim fail independently, and the failure survives the most charitable reading. (1) Listing content: even granting that the envelope's `diagnostics` array is the '根拠一覧', the text rendering of it omits adapter ID, source location and verdict, and the item itself never appears under any project-level heading — so 別紙A's 「adapter ID、source location、diagnostic code、判定値をProject checks配下に表示する」 is not satisfied in text at all. (2) Parity: 「JSONでも同じ根拠一覧を返す」 requires the same evidence list in both formats; JSON exposes adapter + path + locator + byte_range that the text path structurally cannot emit, while the JSON `basis` list itself carries only messages. The two formats therefore list demonstrably different information for the same non-PASS test_traceability, and neither format carries the full required tuple in its basis list. The root cause is a real data loss at crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:663 and 673, where `.map(|diagnostic| diagnostic.message.clone())` drops code, location and adapter before the report boundary — so no renderer downstream can recover them from `basis`.

chain.claim: A test-semantic bundle must include test metadata+source, covered VOs, ALL target implementation sources, static-audit result, and prior audits, with content hashes and revision.
chain.normative_source: Verified in docs/AI並列開発向けテスト検証システム 詳細設計 v0.1.md: (a) §8.1 bundle table L1052 — test-semantic includes "全targetのimplementation construct source全文"; (b) §8.2 JSON schema L1058ff — the field is a plural array "targets": [ { target, source, content_hash } ]; (c) §8.4 L1170 — "subjectsにはバンドル生成時の全対象を記録する。… test-semanticではTest subject・VO・全target"; (d) §8.5 L1180ff — audit validity requires the recorded subject set to match the current audit target set. 基本仕様 §7.3 L403-405 binds an accepted audit to the 完全な対象集合 and requires STALE on any change to that set; 基本仕様 §7.5 L444 states the same all-targets, no-omission rule for multi-target Tests (impl-consistency wording). Multi-target Tests are a first-class concept elsewhere in 詳細設計 (§7 L989: DA-002/DA-003 applied per target; L422: per-target verdict set must be 1:1 with the Test's declared target set).
chain.mechanism: vtest audit bundle --kind test-semantic --test <ID> serializes the judgment input for an external audit agent, and stamps a subjects[] list (kind/id/locator + content hash) that audit submit re-checks and that the accepted Audit Record carries as its binding domain; verify then evaluates semantic_audit from valid (non-stale) audit records.
chain.condition: A Test that legally declares two @vtest.target locators. crates/vtest-adapter-rust/src/discovery.rs:1027-1033 rejects >1 target only when kind does not start with "integration"; with `@vtest.kind integration` two targets scan cleanly (0 diagnostics). Concrete input: TEST-M1-MULTI with @vtest.target src/lib.rs::known and @vtest.target src/lib.rs::also_known.
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs build_bundle(), "test-semantic" arm: lines 1215-1225 resolve `test.targets.first()` only; lines 1237-1242 push exactly one subject_value("target", …); line 1291 emits a singular "target": target_value(root, target). No loop over test.targets, no diagnostic for the dropped ones. Downstream: validate_bundle_subjects() (lines 1853-1933) only re-hashes the subjects that are present — it never checks completeness against the Test's declared target set; crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs evaluate_test_audit() (lines 1355-1442) computes `valid = !subjects.is_empty() && subjects.iter().all(subject_is_current)` — again presence-only, no set-equality with the current target set. (The impl-consistency arm at lines 1420-1500 has the identical .first() defect, which 基本仕様 §7.5 L444 forbids verbatim.)
chain.expected: The bundle for TEST-M1-MULTI contains an implementation source entry and a target subject for BOTH src/lib.rs::known and src/lib.rs::also_known; the accepted Audit Record carries both target subjects; editing either target's body stales the record.
chain.actual: Reproduced: the bundle carries a singular "target" object for src/lib.rs::known only (no "targets" key at all), subjects[] holds exactly 3 entries (test, one target, one vo) — src/lib.rs::also_known appears nowhere, with no warning or diagnostic. audit submit accepted a PASS against that bundle; the written Audit Record's subjects list contains one target locator. verify then reported semantic_audit basis "Test TEST-M1-MULTI: Pass" (record treated as valid, not stale). After changing the body of also_known (a declared audit target), re-running verify still reported "Test TEST-M1-MULTI: Pass" — the record did not go STALE.
chain.negation: System level, not local omission. (1) The state is reachable through the product's own supported path: multi-target is explicitly legal for integration Tests in the adapter, and scan accepted it with zero diagnostics. (2) No later gate rejects it: bundle generation succeeds (no E-SCAN-004 since the first target resolves), audit submit's only structural check (validate_bundle_subjects) validates the subjects that ARE present and cannot notice a missing one, and verify's validity rule is presence-only rather than the §8.5 set-equality rule, so the truncated record counts as a VALID semantic_audit PASS. (3) The harm is exactly what the claim exists to prevent: the audit agent renders a verdict having never seen the second target's implementation source, and that verdict is then bound to an incomplete subject set — proven by mutating also_known and observing the record stay valid, i.e. the omitted target is permanently outside the audit's staleness domain. Nothing downstream can reconstruct the dropped source, so 'all target implementation sources' is violated by construction, and the violation propagates into a false-valid semantic_audit PASS.

chain.claim: VO-INTAKE-08: each spec_refs.spec resolves deterministically to an existing SPEC record and its current source/hash; an unresolvable reference yields MISSING/MISMATCH per 詳細設計 §11.1.1 and can never be PASS.
chain.normative_source: Re-read and verified in the repo. (a) docs/AI並列開発向けテスト検証システム 詳細設計 v0.1.md §11.1.1 (around lines 1360-1371): 'VOの`requirements`またはREQ / VOの`spec_refs.spec`が解決不能なら`MISSING`、`section`が空、参照型またはschemaが矛盾する場合は`MISMATCH`' and '上記がなく、parent、requirements、spec_refsのSPEC entity参照、構造Relationがすべて解決できる場合だけ`PASS`'. (b) Same doc, §11.1 table: vo_decomposition is evaluated at REQ/VO over 'parent・requirements・spec_refs・構造Relation' per §11.1.1. (c) Same doc, diagnostic table line 849: 'E-SCAN-012 | error | REQ / VO のrequirementsまたはspec_refs.specが存在しないentityを参照、またはspec_refs.sectionが空'. §11.1.1 names E-SCAN-012 as one of only four codes that may move this item. So the normative text is explicit, not inferred.
chain.mechanism: Design mechanism: scan emits E-SCAN-012 when a REQ/VO spec_refs.spec (or requirements) references a non-existent entity; verify's vo_decomposition mapping then folds E-SCAN-008 / E-SCAN-012 / subtree-scoped E-SCAN-009 / E-SCAN-010 into MISSING/MISMATCH, and only emits PASS when parent, requirements, spec_refs SPEC entity references and structural Relations all resolve. Secondary mechanism at intake: vtest req/vo add validates --spec via read_spec (crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:3646-3669 spec_refs_from_args), but that guards only the CLI construction path, not the canonical record state.
chain.condition: A canonical REQ or VO record whose spec_refs contains a spec id with no corresponding .verify/spec/<ID>.yaml record. Two reachable constructions, both exercised: (1) create REQ/VO via the CLI against a registered SPEC, then delete the SPEC record file (ordinary filesystem/git operation; there is no `vtest spec remove`, and nothing re-validates); (2) hand-edit the canonical VO YAML to cite SPEC-GHOST (hand-written canonical records are exactly what scan exists to validate).
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:584-598 — vo_decomposition = Fail if any scan diagnostic is_error, else Missing if selection.vo_ids is empty, else Pass with basis 'scan and canonical VO records are structurally readable'. spec_refs is never read on this path. Upstream, crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs validate_req_record (714-767) and validate_vo_record (769-840) check id format/readability/required fields/status/coverage_policy/dimensions only — no spec_refs check; validate_parent_graph (936-995) emits E-SCAN-008 for missing parent and parent cycles only. `grep -rn E-SCAN-012 --include=*.rs crates/` returns zero hits: the code that §11.1.1 depends on does not exist anywhere in the implementation. crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:1327-1362 and 1467-1480 additionally drop unresolvable refs silently in build_bundle ('if let Ok(record) = read_spec(...)'), which is corroborating, not load-bearing.
chain.expected: vo_decomposition = MISSING (spec_refs.spec 解決不能), with an E-SCAN-012 error diagnostic naming the dangling SPEC reference; verify must be non-PASS on that item.
chain.actual: vo_decomposition = PASS with basis 'scan and canonical VO records are structurally readable'; scan emits no error diagnostic at all (only W-SCAN-102 'isolated VO'); scoped `verify --items vo_decomposition` reports result PASS and exits 0. Observed for both the delete-the-SPEC-record construction and the hand-written SPEC-GHOST construction. spec_coverage also stayed PASS after the SPEC record was deleted (its implementation at vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:546-580 only checks 'every selected REQ has ≥1 linked VO'), so nothing else in the aggregate reacted to the dangling reference either.
chain.negation: Negates at SYSTEM level. (1) Reachability: no hand-crafted or unsupported state is required — I created the records through the ordinary CLI and merely deleted the SPEC record file; deletion of a SPEC record while referring REQ/VOs remain is a routine git/refactor outcome, and §11.1.1 itself defines behavior FOR the unresolvable state, i.e. the spec treats it as a reachable state to be diagnosed, not an impossible one. (2) No earlier gate rejects: the intake gate (spec_refs_from_args → read_spec) guards only argument construction at `req add` / `vo add` and never re-runs over existing records; scan, the designated validator of canonical records, has no spec_refs check and no E-SCAN-012 implementation at all; the approval closure check (crates/vtest-store/src/approval.rs:90-158) does fail on an unresolvable spec, but it gates approval/vo_coverage, and vo_decomposition is computed independently of approval state — the reproduction had no approval and still yielded PASS. (3) No aggregate rescue: `verify --items vo_decomposition` is a first-class supported scope, and it returned overall result PASS with exit 0 while a dangling spec_refs.spec existed; even in the full-scope run, vo_decomposition and spec_coverage were both PASS, so the dangling reference produced no non-PASS anywhere attributable to it. The value the spec mandates to be MISSING is emitted as PASS on a supported, fail-closed-intended command path. chain.claim: Among valid audit records on one subject set, any FAIL yields FAIL, else the latest verdict; with no valid record the item is NOT_CHECKED or STALE, never PASS.
chain.normative_source: docs/AI並列開発向けテスト検証システム 詳細設計 v0.1.md §8.5 有効性と多重監査 (L1187, verbatim): 「同一対象に有効なレコードが複数ある場合、FAIL が1件でもあれば FAIL、なければ最新の verdict を採る。」 followed by 「有効なレコードが1件もなければ NOT_CHECKED ... または STALE ...」 and 「再監査・多重監査の回数はツールとして制限しない」. §11.1 チェック項目の評価地点 (L1327ff) binds the item to that rule: semantic_audit = 「有効な test-semantic 監査の合成（§8.5）」 evaluated at TEST; impl_consistency likewise 「有効なimpl-consistency監査を§8.3でCheckValueへ写像して合成」. §7.3/§7.1 (L1009, L1016, L1027) restate the same two-stage selection for the static path («FAIL が1件でもあれば FAIL、なければ最新の有効 record の当該 target verdict を採る»), so the rule is not a one-off phrase.
chain.mechanism: Design mechanism = two-stage effective-record selection per subject set: (1) drop records whose subjects are not current (STALE); (2) among the survivors, FAIL dominates, otherwise pick the chronologically latest record's verdict. The codebase already implements exactly this mechanism for the static kind: crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:1115 compare_audit_recency (RFC3339 instant, id tiebreak) used at lib.rs:936 and lib.rs:962 via .max_by(...), witnessed by TEST-VERIFY-008 (FAIL wins) and TEST-VERIFY-015 (latest by real instant across offsets), both targeting evaluate_static_audit.
chain.condition: One Test whose subject set is unchanged, carrying two VALID test-semantic audit records with identical subjects: an older record with verdict UNKNOWN and a newer record with verdict PASS. §8.5 explicitly allows unlimited re-audit, and audit subjects (test/target/vo/req/spec/config — parse_audit_subjects + subject_is_current, lib.rs:1559-1596) contain nothing bundle- or record-specific, so both records stay valid simultaneously.
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:648 ("semantic_audit" => evaluate_test_audit(root, layout, scan, "test-semantic")) → evaluate_test_audit (lib.rs:1355-1440). Records are grouped per test into per_test (id, valid, verdict); validity is computed at lib.rs:1385-1389; the surviving valid verdicts are reduced at lib.rs:1414-1425 by `valid.iter().map(|(_,_,verdict)| *verdict).fold(CheckValue::Pass, combine_values)`. combine_values (lib.rs:1854-1876) is a severity-rank max (Fail 8 > Mismatch 7 > Missing 6 > Stale 5 > NotExecuted 4 > NotChecked 3 > Unknown 2 > Pass 1) with Pass as identity. audited_at is never read on this path — compare_audit_recency has no call site inside evaluate_test_audit (only lib.rs:936/962 in the static path). The same defect applies to impl_consistency (lib.rs:649, same function) and to the vo-coverage fold at lib.rs:1330.
chain.expected: Per §8.5 via §11.1: no FAIL among the valid records, therefore the effective verdict is the latest valid record's verdict = PASS, so the semantic_audit item for that Test is PASS and the scoped verify/report result is PASS.
chain.actual: combine_values folds severity-max over all valid verdicts irrespective of audited_at: fold(Pass, Unknown) = Unknown, then combine(Unknown, Pass) = Unknown. The item value is UNKNOWN and the scoped report result is UNKNOWN. Note the scope precisely: the FAIL-dominance conjunct IS satisfied (Fail has the top rank) and the degenerate conjunct IS satisfied (empty valid set yields Stale, non-empty record set with no valid record never yields Pass — lib.rs:1410-1413). The broken conjunct is exactly «else the latest verdict»: on this path chronology is never consulted, so an older non-PASS verdict is never superseded.
chain.negation: System level, not local omission. (a) Reachability: the state is constructible with the shipped CLI alone (two audit submit calls on the same unchanged Test), and §8.5 positively sanctions repeated audits, so nothing in the spec forbids the input. (b) No later gate rescues it: semantic_audit is a terminal check-item value — §11.1 evaluates it at TEST and §7.x aggregation only folds item values upward, so an UNKNOWN item can only make the aggregate worse, never restore PASS. The repro observes the item value itself (`semantic_audit: UNKNOWN`, `result: UNKNOWN`) with both records listed as valid (no `(stale)` marker), so no validity gate rejected the older record first. (c) The 'severity-max is merely conservative / fail-closed, so it is not a violation' defense fails on the spec's own text: 「最新の verdict を採る」 is an imperative selection rule, not a lower bound, and under severity-max an older UNKNOWN becomes permanently un-supersedeable short of deleting the record — which directly negates §8.5's unlimited-re-audit provision whose only purpose is to let a later audit replace an earlier undecided one. A rule that can never be discharged by the mechanism the same section grants is broken, not conservatively approximated. (d) It is a divergence, not spec ambiguity: the identical rule is implemented with real recency ordering in evaluate_static_audit (lib.rs:936/962, TEST-VERIFY-008/015), so the same normative sentence is honoured on one path and dropped on the other. Therefore the claim's «else the latest verdict» half is false of the running system for semantic_audit (and impl_consistency).

chain.claim: Unresolvable targets produce no impl-consistency bundle and no auto-selected candidate; absent target yields MISSING, ambiguous resolution MISMATCH, never collapsed to one value.
chain.normative_source: Verified verbatim in three layers. 基本仕様 §7.5 (docs/AI並列開発向けテスト検証システム 基本仕様 v0.1.md): 「targetを一意に解決できない場合はバンドルを生成せず、候補のいずれも選択しない。対象が存在しない場合は`MISSING`、複数候補により曖昧な場合は`MISMATCH`とする。」 詳細設計 §8.1 (docs/AI並列開発向けテスト検証システム 詳細設計 v0.1.md): 「`impl-consistency` のバンドル生成時、宣言targetのいずれか…を解決できない場合はバンドルを生成せず、候補のいずれも選択しない…対象が存在しない場合（E-SCAN-004…）は`MISSING`、恒久SRC IDの衝突により複数候補で曖昧な場合（E-SCAN-011）は`MISMATCH`」。詳細設計 §8.3: 「target解決不能（対象なしの`MISSING`、曖昧の`MISMATCH`。§8.1）、監査未実施の`NOT_CHECKED`…をこの写像で上書きしない。」 詳細設計 §11.1 table row for `impl_consistency`: 「監査FAILはMISMATCH、対象シンボル不在はMISSING、曖昧な解決（E-SCAN-011）はMISMATCH」。
chain.mechanism: Core-owned cross-entity resolution (crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:1276-1334 `cross_entity_diagnostics`) is meant to separate the two failure kinds: E-SCAN-011 for a permanent SRC ID claimed by >1 Source Target, E-SCAN-004 for a Test target that does not resolve to exactly one source. `vtest audit bundle --kind impl-consistency` must refuse to emit a bundle and must not pick a candidate when any declared target is unresolvable; `vtest verify` must map the absent kind to impl_consistency = MISSING and the ambiguous kind to MISMATCH, and the audit-verdict mapping must not overwrite those states.
chain.condition: Two minimal isolated Rust projects with the m1 base config and one VO record. (A) absent: src/lib.rs has only `known()`, Test TEST-ABSENT declares `@vtest.target src/lib.rs::gone`. (B) ambiguous: two constructs both carry `/// @vtest.src-id SRC-DUAL`, Test TEST-AMBIG declares `@vtest.target SRC-DUAL`.
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:1317-1334 (target resolved only when count==1; otherwise E-SCAN-004, same code+message for 0 and >1); crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:67-80 `find_target_source` uses `.iter().find(...)` — first match wins, no arity check; crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:1418-1431 (impl-consistency bundle: `test.targets.first().and_then(|t| find_target_source(scan, t))`, only the None arm fails with E-SCAN-004); crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:1520-1552 (--vo arm, same first-match); crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:649 → 1355-1442 `evaluate_test_audit("impl-consistency")` derives the value purely from audit records (no record ⇒ CheckValue::NotChecked); grep confirms E-SCAN-004 / E-SCAN-011 are consumed nowhere in crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs (only E-SCAN-002/003 and W-SCAN-101/E-SCAN-007 in `evaluate_test_traceability`, lines 658-676).
chain.expected: (A) absent: no bundle; impl_consistency = MISSING. (B) ambiguous: no bundle and no candidate selected; impl_consistency = MISMATCH. The two values never collapse into one, and the audit-verdict mapping never overwrites them.
chain.actual: (A) absent: bundle refused (E-SCAN-004, exit 2) — the bundle half holds here; but verify reports impl_consistency = NOT_CHECKED ('audit missing'), not MISSING. (B) ambiguous: `audit bundle --kind impl-consistency --test TEST-AMBIG` returned ok:true, exit 0, and wrote a bundle whose target subject auto-selected one of the two candidates (`rust-cargo::src/lib.rs::also_known`), with E-SCAN-011/E-SCAN-004 demoted to non-blocking diagnostics; verify then reports impl_consistency = NOT_CHECKED, identical to (A); after submitting a PASS impl-consistency result against that bundle (`audit submit`, exit 0), verify reports impl_consistency = PASS.
chain.negation: Every conjunct of the claim fails at system level and no other gate rescues them. (i) 'no bundle / no auto-selected candidate' is falsified in the ambiguous branch: the bundle command succeeds (exit 0) and silently picks the first of two SRC-DUAL candidates, because the CLI resolves targets via `find_target_source`'s first-match instead of consulting the scan's arity-checked resolution. (ii) 'absent → MISSING, ambiguous → MISMATCH, never collapsed' is falsified because the verify layer never reads E-SCAN-004 / E-SCAN-011 at all: both branches yield the single value NOT_CHECKED, and once an audit exists over the illegitimate bundle the ambiguous case rises to PASS — exactly the overwrite §8.3 forbids. (iii) No other gate rejects the state first: scan exits 1 but verify still runs and emits a full report; the aggregate result is NG only via `vo_decomposition = FAIL` with basis 'scan emitted an error diagnostic' (crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:585) — and 詳細設計 §11.1.1 explicitly forbids target-resolution errors from affecting `vo_decomposition` ('target解決…の各errorは対応するTest・実行・Evidence dimensionへ写像し、`vo_decomposition`を変更しない'), so the only thing making the run NG is itself a mapping violation and it provides neither the MISSING/MISMATCH distinction nor any block on bundle/submit. The state is trivially reachable from ordinary annotated sources. The cited candidate's one inaccuracy — asserting the 'no bundle / no candidate' half holds — understates the defect: that half also breaks in the ambiguous branch.

chain.claim: Core materializes Test Entities from the adapter's normalized logical fields only and never interprets adapter-owned declaration syntax or placement (comment forms, decorators, attributes, manifest syntax). Structural/negative facet: core contains no interpretation of those forms.
chain.normative_source: VERIFIED verbatim in the docs, not merely as cited. 基本仕様 §6.1 (docs/AI並列開発向けテスト検証システム 基本仕様 v0.1.md): 『adapterは固有の記述場所と構文から、§6.2の論理fieldとTest constructのSource Locationを決定論的に導出する。coreはadapter固有のcomment形式、decorator、attribute、manifest構文を解釈しない。』 詳細設計 §4.1: 『coreはsource declarationの構文と配置を解釈せず、adapterが返したTest Entity、…を検証・統合する。』 詳細設計 §1.1 makes 'core' concrete and non-conceptual: crates/vtest-adapter-rust is 'rust-cargo discovery/audit/operations/runner/coverage', while 『vtest-scan、vtest-audit、vtest-exec はadapterを選択・委譲するorchestrationであり』. 基本仕様 §8.1/§8.2 assign generating/updating the metadata declaration to the adapter (『adapterが現状との差分を計算してTest constructとmetadata宣言を更新し、coreが結果を再スキャンして検証する』). 詳細設計 §4.2 normatively fixes the rust-cargo declaration form as 『テスト関数直前の doc comment（`///` または `/** */`）内の行』. 要件定義 §7.1 (checked, per the VO refs) is about test_traceability only and carves out no exception for Structured Test Operations.
chain.mechanism: Declaration syntax and placement are adapter-owned: SourceDiscoveryAdapter normalizes source declarations into the logical field set (id, covers[], targets[], intent, input?, expect?, kind?, cases[], related[]); core validates/hashes/materializes from those fields and re-scans after an operation. Rendering the declaration back into source is therefore an adapter responsibility — which the create path honours (render_form_template lives in crates/vtest-adapter-rust/src/operations_support.rs:378).
chain.condition: Any `vtest test edit` on a rust-cargo Test. Two inputs: (a) control — a Test declared with `///` doc comments; (b) counterexample — a Test declared with the equally-normative `/** … */` block doc comment form (詳細設計 §4.2), correctly discovered and materialized by the adapter, then edited via `vtest test edit <ID> --set intent=…`.
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:463 (TestCommand::Edit) → vtest_scan::operations::edit_test → crates/vtest-scan/src/operations.rs:235 `render_edited_test(&normalized_current, &current, &desired, body)` → crates/vtest-scan/src/operations.rs:510-590. That function, defined in the CORE crate vtest-scan, (i) partitions the construct's lines by `trimmed.starts_with("///")` and `trimmed.contains("@vtest.")` into free_before / annotation / free_after — i.e. it decides declaration placement; (ii) rewrites `fn <selector>`; (iii) emits literal `/// @vtest.id|covers|target|intent|input|expect|kind|case|related` lines. `normalize_body` (operations.rs:592+) additionally synthesizes Rust brace syntax in core. Contrast: the create path calls the adapter's render_form_template (crates/vtest-adapter-rust/src/operations_support.rs:378). vtest_adapter_api::StructuredTestAdapter (crates/vtest-adapter-api/src/lib.rs:438-441) exposes only built_in_form_kinds/accepts_compatibility_form — there is no rendering method, so no adapter path for edit-time declaration rendering exists. NOTE: the candidate's sub-argument that the hard import `use vtest_adapter_rust::operations_support::*` (operations.rs:12) and RUST_ADAPTER_ID (:15) are themselves violations is WRONG and is not relied on here — 詳細設計 §1.1 explicitly permits `scan / audit / exec → adapter-rust`. The violation is that render_edited_test is DEFINED in core, not that core imports the adapter.
chain.expected: Per §6.1/§4.1/§8.1/§8.2: core hands the desired logical fields to the adapter, the adapter renders the declaration in whatever form it owns (`///` or `/** */`), core re-scans and verifies. Core never needs to know that rust-cargo declarations are `///`-prefixed doc-comment lines placed immediately before the fn. Consequently Edit Test works uniformly for every declaration form 詳細設計 §4.2 admits.
chain.actual: Core owns the syntax and knows only the `///` form. Control (`///`, TEST-ADD-002): edit succeeds — core-authored `/// @vtest.*` lines are written to disk, exit 0. Counterexample (`/** … */`, TEST-ADD-001): scan discovers and materializes the entity with zero diagnostics (byte_range 49..268 starting at the `/**`), but render_edited_test's `starts_with("///")` test fails on every declaration line, so the whole block doc comment falls into `tail`/`function` and core prepends a second, `///`-form declaration. `--dry-run` returns ok:true with that duplicated/corrupted `rendered` payload and NO gate at all. The non-dry-run write is caught after the fact by verify_edit → rollback (operations.rs:272-276), which restores the file and fails with E-OP-003 『edited Test `TEST-ADD-001` was not recognized by the scanner』 (exit 2). chain.negation: System level, on both facets, and the rollback gate does NOT save it. (1) Structural facet: the claim is negated unconditionally by construction — a core crate contains, on the sole production path of a spec-mandated operation (基本仕様 §8.1 Edit Test), the interpretation of an adapter-owned comment form and its placement rule, plus generation of that same syntax. Reachability is proven, not argued: the control edit completed with exit 0 and wrote core-generated `///` lines to disk. No gate can reject this state because executing it IS the operation. (2) Positive/functional facet: because syntax knowledge sits in core rather than the adapter, core's knowledge is a strict subset of the adapter's, and Edit Test fails 100% of the time for the `/** */` form that 詳細設計 §4.2 normatively admits and that the adapter demonstrably discovers cleanly. (3) The verify_edit/rollback gate is containment, not a rejecting gate in the protocol's sense: it fires AFTER core's syntax interpretation has already produced the wrong bytes and written them, and it converts the defect into an outright failure of the normatively required operation — that is the contradiction's symptom, not its refutation. Branch context (feature/adapter-separation-alpha2-implementation; discovery.rs:638 comments that this boundary 'moves wholesale to vtest-adapter-rust in the next step') shows the team knows the migration is mid-flight, but a non-normative refactoring plan cannot suspend 基本仕様 §6.1.

chain.claim: VO-EXIST-08: An incomplete or unparseable discovery result is never treated as a complete 0-test discovery; the affected verification becomes UNKNOWN and test_traceability = UNKNOWN, which cannot PASS.
chain.normative_source: Verified in the normative docs, not just the ontology. 詳細設計 v0.1 line 587 (§5.1): 「adapterが解析不能または不完全なbatchを返した場合、coreは対応する検証を`UNKNOWN`とし、Test 0件の完全なdiscoveryとして扱わない。」 詳細設計 line 1378 (§11.1, the test_traceability judgment list): 「discovery結果が不完全または解析不能なら`UNKNOWN`とし、PASSにしない。」 詳細設計 line 838: E-SCAN-001 = 「adapterのsource構文解析失敗（DiscoveryBatchは`Incomplete`）」; line 872: 「解析エラーのファイルはE-SCAN-001を返し、batchをIncompleteとする」. 別紙C §18.3.1: 「adapter discoveryの失敗をTest 0件の正常scanとして扱わない。」 and 「`vtest scan` / `doctor`はE-ADAPTER-* / E-CONFIG-*による操作拒否をexit 2、完了したscanのE-SCAN-*をexit 1、errorなしをexit 0にする。」 That exit partition is decisive for scoping: E-SCAN-001 is a COMPLETED scan (exit 1), not an operation rejection (exit 2), so an Incomplete batch is a legal protocol outcome that must still yield a scan result and must map the affected verification item to UNKNOWN. It also shows VO-EXIST-07 (E-ADAPTER-*/registry/config -> operation error, exit 2) and VO-EXIST-08 (adapter RETURNS an Incomplete/unparseable batch -> UNKNOWN, exit 1) govern disjoint triggers, so the candidate's 'same trigger, conflicting prescriptions' worry is not a spec conflict.
chain.mechanism: DiscoveryBatch.completeness (crates/vtest-adapter-api/src/lib.rs:107,113) is the adapter->core incompleteness signal. On a per-file read/parse failure the adapter must (a) emit E-SCAN-001 and (b) set completeness = Incomplete (詳細設計 line 872). Core must then still materialize/complete the scan (exit 1) while carrying incompleteness forward so verify's test_traceability evaluates to UNKNOWN instead of PASS (詳細設計 line 1378).
chain.condition: A project whose adapter scan input contains at least one Rust source file that cannot be parsed or read, with no other findings — discovery is provably incomplete and yields 0 discovered Tests. Concretely: `.verify/` created by `vtest init`, plus `src/broken.rs` containing syntactically invalid Rust.
chain.impl_path: Three legs, all re-read directly; the decisive one is NOT among the candidate's citations. (1) crates/vtest-adapter-rust/src/discovery.rs:743-765 emits Diagnostic::error("E-SCAN-001", ...) on read/parse failure, then Scanner::finish() at crates/vtest-adapter-rust/src/discovery.rs:1176-1185 hard-codes `completeness: DiscoveryCompleteness::Complete` unconditionally — the shipped adapter NEVER reports Incomplete; a grep over crates/ shows the only `DiscoveryCompleteness::Incomplete` construction anywhere is a unit-test fixture at crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:1651. (2) crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:97-102 `materialize_discovery_batch` rejects any non-Complete batch via malformed_adapter_output -> AdapterError::MalformedOutput / E-ADAPTER-002 (crates/vtest-adapter-api/src/lib.rs:240), destroying the only spec-legal Incomplete path; the test at crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:1650-1655 freezes that as intended. (3) crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:659-685 `evaluate_test_traceability` filters only E-SCAN-002/E-SCAN-003 -> Mismatch and W-SCAN-101/E-SCAN-007 -> Missing, else Pass; E-SCAN-001 is in neither filter and there is no CheckValue::Unknown branch. ScanResult carries no completeness field at all (crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:84-90,143), so the incompleteness fact is structurally unavailable to verify.
chain.expected: Scan completes with exit 1 carrying E-SCAN-001, and `vtest verify` reports test_traceability = UNKNOWN (never PASS), with the discovery not presented as a complete 0-test result.
chain.actual: Scan completes with exit 1 and E-SCAN-001 (correct per 別紙C), but the batch is flagged Complete, so the ScanResult is a fully materialized 'complete' 0-test discovery (summary: files 0, tests 0, sources 0). `vtest verify` then returns test_traceability = PASS with basis "all 0 discovered managed Test(s) are structurally traceable". Scoped to the item (`verify --items test_traceability`) the whole run is ok=true, exit code 0, report result = PASS, with E-SCAN-001 still in diagnostics. CheckValue::Unknown for this item is unreachable by construction. CORRECTION TO THE CANDIDATE: it characterized the divergence as 'stricter fail-closed (operation error), not fail-open'. That is wrong for the reachable path. The E-ADAPTER-002 abort it cites (crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:98-102 plus the null-data envelope at crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:2480-2494) is real code but reachable only from test fixtures, because no shipped adapter ever sets Incomplete. The reachable production behavior is fail-OPEN: PASS on an unparseable source tree.
chain.negation: System-level negation holds on all three counts the protocol requires. (a) Reachability: the triggering state is trivially constructible in any real project (one unparseable .rs file) and was reproduced end-to-end with the prebuilt binary in an isolated project. (b) The claim's observable is the per-item check value, and it reads PASS — the exact value 詳細設計 line 1378 forbids (「PASSにしない」) — and the scan is exactly the 「Test 0件の完全なdiscovery」 that line 587 and 別紙C §18.3.1 forbid. (c) No other gate necessarily rejects. At full scope the overall report is FAIL, but solely via vo_decomposition's blanket `scan.diagnostics.iter().any(is_error)` -> FAIL at crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:583-590 with basis "scan emitted an error diagnostic" — a mapping 詳細設計 §11.1.1 explicitly forbids (「Test ID、Test metadata、target解決、adapter source parse、Evidenceの各errorは対応するTest・実行・Evidence dimensionへ写像し、`vo_decomposition`を変更しない」), so that FAIL is accidental masking by a spec-violating catch-all rather than a normative gate (raised only to dispose of the 'another gate rejects first' objection, not as a second finding). And item scoping is itself spec-sanctioned — §11.1 discusses `--items` for this very item — under which `verify --items test_traceability` yields ok=true / exit 0 / result PASS with zero masking. That scoped run is an unmasked system-level counterexample: a project whose discovery provably failed to parse its only source file is certified PASS on the very item the spec says can never PASS in that state.

chain.claim: Static rules mark FAIL only for deterministically confirmed violations; verdicts a rule cannot determine are UNKNOWN, never FAIL and never treated as no-violation.
chain.normative_source: VERIFIED, and it is two-layered and mutually tense. (a) PRINCIPLE, higher precedence: 要件定義 §11 (L479-508) defines the violation classes semantically — '明らかに意味のないテスト' / 'その他、同様に検証結果が対象実装の正しさに依存しない構造'; 基本仕様 §7.2 (L370-371) '判定は保守的に行う。決定論的に確定できる違反のみ `FAIL` とし、確定できないものは `UNKNOWN` として意味監査へ送る。'; 詳細設計 §7.1 (L959-960) '**決定論的に確定できる違反のみ FAIL とする。**解析の限界で確定できない場合は FAIL ではなく UNKNOWN とし、意味監査へ委ねる'; 別紙C §18.3.2 (L94) '確定違反だけをFAILとし、解析限界をUNKNOWNとして保持する。' (b) RULE ROW, lower precedence but more specific: 詳細設計 §7.2 table L985 — '| DA-006 検証構文なし | 関数内に assert 相当が1つも存在しない | FAIL条件: 該当 | UNKNOWNへ退避する例: なし |'. Note DA-006 is NOT in 基本仕様 §7.2's enumerated minimum rule list (which names only DA-001..DA-005 equivalents); it exists only from 詳細設計 down. 実装スケジュール L7-14 fixes doc precedence 要件定義 > 基本仕様 > 詳細設計本冊 > 別紙A/C, but that clause is conditional on a conflict existing — it does not itself decide whether one exists here.
chain.mechanism: §7.2 defines a shared 'assert相当の構文' set (std assert macros + config `assertion_macros` + #[should_panic] + .unwrap()/.expect()/? + Result-returning-and-can-Err). DA-006 fires when that set is empty within 関数内. Crucially, the design fixes per-rule analysis boundaries asymmetrically: DA-002 explicitly walks '関数本体および同一ファイル内の呼出先 helper（1段）', and DA-002/DA-003 have declared UNKNOWN escapes for boundary-crossing cases; DA-004/DA-005/DA-006 are declared 'なし'. §7.1's designated destination for an undeterminable verdict is UNKNOWN → 意味監査; and §7.2 L996 states DA-001〜DA-006 FAIL tests are excluded from the semantic-audit bundle by default.
chain.condition: A #[test] fn whose body contains NO assert-like syntax (no assert macro, no #[should_panic], no .unwrap()/.expect()/`?`, not Result-returning) and whose verification is delegated to a plain call to a same-file assert helper fn that itself contains the assert. Example: `#[test] fn delegating_test() { assert_add_is_sum(); }` with `fn assert_add_is_sum() { assert_eq!(add(1,2), 3); }`. This is the exact shape measured in this repo: docs/reports/w8-dogfood-findings.md L81-85 records TEST-CLI-022/023/060 delegating to assert_adapter_usage_error / assert_ok / assert_tree_child (3/3 individually confirmed); the helper is real, e.g. crates/vtest-cli/tests/adapter_acceptance.rs:761.
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-adapter-rust/src/static_audit.rs:1190-1199 `has_assert_like(item: &ItemFn, ...)` — collect_assertions + should_panic + VerificationSyntaxVisitor (unwrap/expect/`?`) + returns_result_and_can_err, ALL scoped to the passed ItemFn; there is no helper-resolution hop (contrast rule_da002 at :344 and rule_da003 at :691, which do `call_facts(candidates[0], ...)` on the same-file helper). crates/vtest-adapter-rust/src/static_audit.rs:1800-1812 emits DA-006 as `verdict: if has_assert { AuditVerdict::Pass } else { AuditVerdict::Fail }` — a two-valued expression with no AuditVerdict::Unknown arm at all. Downstream: crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:1207-1211 skips test-semantic bundle generation when the static audit verdict is Fail unless --include-failed.
chain.expected: Under the §7.1 / 基本仕様 L371 principle: the rule cannot see inside the helper, therefore it cannot determine whether the test verifies anything, therefore DA-006 must yield UNKNOWN and the case must be routed to 意味監査 — never FAIL. (Under the competing reading, expected = FAIL, because §7.2 L985 declares the class syntactically and declares no UNKNOWN escape.)
chain.actual: REPRODUCED in an isolated project. TEST-X-001 (helper-delegated): DA-001 PASS, DA-002 UNKNOWN, DA-003 UNKNOWN ('target result crosses a same-file helper boundary'), DA-004 PASS, DA-005 PASS, **DA-006 FAIL ('no assert-like syntax is present')** → record verdict FAIL → `verify --items static_audit` = FAIL → `audit bundle --kind test-semantic` returns {"skipped":true, reason "static audit verdict is FAIL; pass --include-failed to force a bundle"}. Semantically identical control TEST-X-002 (same assertion written inline): DA-006 PASS, record verdict UNKNOWN, bundle GENERATED. So on one and the same input the implementation simultaneously reports DA-003 = UNKNOWN because the helper boundary blocks it, and DA-006 = FAIL asserting verification is definitively absent — and the FAIL closes the very 意味監査 route §7.1 designates for undeterminable cases.
chain.negation: CONDITIONAL — this is why the outcome is NEEDS-SPEC-JUDGMENT rather than CONFIRMED. The system-level consequence is real and not neutralized: no other gate rejects the state first (the FAIL is produced on a well-formed, non-malformed record, survives §8.5 effective-record selection as FAIL-dominant, becomes static_audit = FAIL at verify time, and additionally suppresses the semantic-audit bundle), and the state is trivially reachable (reproduced in minutes). So IF §7.1's '違反' denotes the semantic defect that 要件定義 §11 enumerates ('検証結果が対象実装の正しさに依存しない構造'), then actual negates the claim: the analysis provably cannot determine that defect here — its sibling rule DA-003 says so in the same record — yet DA-006 emits FAIL, i.e. FAIL on an undeterminable case, exactly what the claim forbids, and the mandated UNKNOWN→意味監査 escape is not merely skipped but affirmatively blocked. BUT IF DA-006's violation class is its own syntactic predicate as 詳細設計 §7.2 L985 literally writes it ('関数内に assert 相当が1つも存在しない'; rule name '検証構文なし' = no verification *syntax*; 'UNKNOWNへ退避する例: なし'), then that predicate is decidable and TRUE for this input, the FAIL IS a deterministically confirmed violation of the declared class, and no negation occurs — the complaint degrades to 'the declared class over-approximates the intent', a design-quality defect, not a determinism contradiction. The implementation faithfully executes the most specific normative text that exists for DA-006, so the contradiction, if any, lives between spec layers rather than between spec and code. The precedence chain in 実装スケジュール L7-14 (要件定義 > 基本仕様 > 詳細設計) would resolve it in favour of the first reading, but only once a conflict is agreed to exist, which is precisely the disputed point; and 実装スケジュール L18 / §17 direct that '上位仕様と詳細設計で観測可能な挙動が矛盾する' be recorded and stopped on, not absorbed in the implementation. The second facet of the VO ('UNKNOWN never read as no-violation') is not implicated at all — UNKNOWN is correctly kept non-PASS throughout.

dossiers.spec_gap:
The corpus supports two incompatible readings of what DA-006's FAIL asserts, and both rest on explicit normative text rather than silence.

READING A — rule-relative determinism (DA-006's class is syntactic). 詳細設計 §7.2 L985 defines DA-006 as '検証構文なし / 関数内に assert 相当が1つも存在しない', FAIL条件 '該当', UNKNOWNへ退避する例 'なし'. The rule name says *syntax*. Its analysis boundary is 関数内 — deliberately narrower than DA-002's, which the same table spells out as '関数本体および同一ファイル内の呼出先 helper（1段）', showing the author distinguished boundaries per rule on purpose. The predicate is fully decidable, so §7.1's 'confirmed violations only' is satisfied and the 'なし' column is an affirmative design decision, not an oversight. Supporting: DA-004/DA-005 are also 'なし' and are genuinely syntax-closed. Under A the implementation is conformant and this candidate is a rule-precision complaint.

READING B — violation-relative determinism (DA-006's class is the semantic defect). 要件定義 §11 defines the violation universe semantically ('明らかに意味のないテスト', 'その他、同様に検証結果が対象実装の正しさに依存しない構造'), 基本仕様 L370-371 orders 保守的 judgement with 'confirmed violations only → FAIL, otherwise UNKNOWN → 意味監査', 詳細設計 §7.1 repeats it, 別紙C §18.3.2 L94-95 adds '正常Testは違反なしとなり'. A helper-delegating test IS a 正常 Test whose correctness does depend on the implementation, so FAILing it is FAIL on a case the rule could not confirm — an analysis limit, identical in kind to the one DA-003 answers with UNKNOWN on the same input in the same record. Under B, §7.2 L985's 'なし' is itself the defect, and 実装スケジュール L7-14's precedence (要件定義 > 基本仕様 > 詳細設計) subordinates it.

The corpus contains no clause that says a §7 rule row may narrow the §7.1 principle, and none that says the principle overrides an explicit rule row; the precedence list only tells you who wins ONCE a conflict is granted, which is the contested question. Note also that DA-006 has no counterpart in 基本仕様 §7.2's enumerated minimum rule set (which covers only the DA-001..DA-005 equivalents), so no higher-layer text fixes DA-006's class at all — the gap is that the highest normative statement about DA-006 is exactly the row under dispute.

Owner decision required, in the shape of one of: (i) affirm Reading A and record in §7.1 that rules may define syntactic violation classes whose FAIL is confirmed by construction (accepting that helper-delegating tests are rejected before 意味監査 by design, and ideally noting it in 別紙C); or (ii) affirm Reading B and amend the §7.2 DA-006 row to add an UNKNOWN escape for 'assert 相当が本体に無いが、同一ファイル内 helper 呼出が存在する' — mirroring the DA-002 one-hop boundary and the DA-003 helper-boundary UNKNOWN that the implementation already emits — which also requires a rule-set version bump (§7.2) so existing records go STALE. (b) docs/…別紙C 受入仕様 v0.1.md L166 (§18.3.5 verify・report, = SPEC-ACCEPT §18.3.5, the VO's first ref), verbatim: 「text treeのancestor continuation、middle child、last childを一意なbranch記号で描画する。」 別紙C does not compete with 別紙A — it states the same rule at acceptance level, so there is no dual reading. 別紙A L215-221 additionally carries a worked sample output that itself uses `│     ├─` continuation and `└─` for last siblings, matching the prose. TEST-CLI-060/080 do not appear anywhere in docs/*.md.
chain.mechanism: Per 別紙A the prefix is composed level-by-level from ANCESTOR state only (`│  ` if that ancestor has following siblings, else three spaces), and the branch mark (`├─ ` middle / `└─ ` last) is computed from the CURRENT node's own sibling position and applied to that node's own line — including top-level nodes. The two concerns are deliberately separated so an ancestor's own mark never propagates downward. verify/report serialize `VerificationReport.tree: Vec<VerificationNode>` (crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:79, node struct L63-70 with `items` and `children`), and the CLI text renderer walks that tree.
chain.condition: Any `vtest verify` or `vtest report` run in the default `--format text` (OutputFormat::Text is the clap default, crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:41; emit_text dispatch at L3854) whose report tree is non-empty. Minimum trigger: a bare `vtest init` project — the single top-level node scope:PROJECT is the LAST (only) sibling and carries item children. Richer trigger: one REQ with two child VOs, which exercises middle-vs-last siblings and depth-2 descendant node lines in one output.

For the bare-init case: `└─ scope:PROJECT`, then `   ├─ spec_coverage` … `   └─ test_traceability`.
chain.actual: Observed from the prebuilt binary (see repro). Bare init: `├─ scope:PROJECT` (top-level last sibling gets `├─ `), then twelve identical `├─ │  ├─ <item>` lines, the last one `├─ │  ├─ test_traceability   PASS`. Two-VO case: `├─ req:REQ-A`, `├─ │  ├─ spec_coverage`, `├─ │  vo:VO-A`, `├─ │  │  ├─ vo_decomposition`…, `├─ │  vo:VO-B`, `├─ │  │  ├─ …`. VO-A (middle) and VO-B (last) are byte-identical in prefix. (2) 'ancestor's mark never inherited': L3962's `format!("{prefix}│  ")` is textual accumulation onto the parent's complete prefix, so the root's `├─ ` from L3886 is structurally guaranteed to prefix every descendant line — this is not an edge case but the only possible behavior. No other gate mediates: emit_text (L3854) is reached for every non-quiet text-format run, there is no second renderer, no config flag suppresses the tree, and no validation rejects the report before rendering — the tree IS the product being emitted. The state-anchored reading is the only one that stands: the claim says 'while … mismatches', §3.1 keys on the mismatch state, and the two invalidation sentences (audit / Approval) sit in ONE §11.4 paragraph — the Approval one is implemented state-anchored against `record.sha256`, so the audit sentence in the same paragraph cannot be re-read as event-anchored.
chain.mechanism: Audit freshness is hash binding: an Audit Record stores a subject set at bundle time and verify recomputes each subject's current hash (§8.5/§11). For the `spec` subject the implementation deliberately binds the CURRENT Specification source bytes, never `SpecRecord.sha256` — crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:1327-1331 carries the design comment "Bind the current Specification source so a body that moved after registration is detected, not the frozen registration snapshot". The Approval closure uses the opposite mechanism: crates/vtest-store/src/approval.rs:145-152 compares `hash_specification_source(&source)` against `record.sha256` and fails closed with 'recorded sha256 does not match the current Specification source'.
chain.condition: Drift the SPEC source BEFORE the audit is bundled, i.e. produce an audit inside the open W-SCAN-104 window: (1) register SPEC-X at source hash H0; (2) edit docs/spec.md to H1 (record still says H0 → W-SCAN-104 live, mismatch state active); (3) `vtest audit bundle --kind impl-consistency` — the spec subject is recorded as H1; (4) `vtest audit submit`; (5) `vtest verify`.

In the vo-coverage run the same happened (audit listed without '(stale)'); `vo_coverage` only fell to MISSING because of the separate approval gate. The code comment's rationale is itself off-target: current-source binding detects a body that moved after the AUDIT, not after REGISTRATION, so the drift-before-bundle window is exactly what it fails to cover. Generate and accept a `test-semantic` (and `impl-consistency`) audit for it, then edit ONLY the body of the second declared target (`second`), leaving the Test source, the first target, the VO record and config untouched.

chain.negation: System level, not a local omission. (a) The state is reachable through spec-sanctioned operations only: a multi-target integration Test is explicitly allowed (詳細設計 line 523 / 別紙A §14.3), and every step used (`audit bundle` -> `audit submit` -> edit source -> `verify`) is a normal tool operation; submit accepted the truncated bundle with zero diagnostics. chain.claim: spec_coverage PASSes only via a valid COMPLETE spec-coverage audit; REQ existence, unconfirmed intake, or empty SPEC/REQ sets are MISSING or non-PASS, never promoted to PASS (VO-PLAN-02, requirement REQ-VERIFICATION-PLANNING).

chain.mechanism: `vtest audit bundle --kind spec-coverage --spec SPEC-X` produces a bundle bound to the current SPEC source hash plus the complete set of active REQs referencing that SPEC; an AI/human auditor submits a verdict COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE/UNKNOWN which maps to PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN; verify then reads that valid (non-stale) spec-coverage Audit record and only then may set spec_coverage = PASS. Empty registered-Specification set, or absent/stale audit, must degrade to MISSING (fail-closed).
chain.condition: Any project where at least one active REQ exists and every selected REQ is referenced by at least one VO, while (a) no spec-coverage audit record exists (it cannot exist), and (b) either a registered Specification contains requirements that were never intaken into any active REQ, or no Specification is registered at all. chain.claim: A Form lacking `adapter` resolves only if exactly one registered Structured Test adapter's built-in kind declaration or deterministic schema compatibility matcher accepts it; 0 or 2+ matches must reject the operation without touching files, and core must never fall back to rust-cargo on an unknown kind.

chain.mechanism: vtest-adapter-api defines the exact mechanism the spec names: `pub trait StructuredTestAdapter { fn built_in_form_kinds(&self) -> Vec<String>; fn accepts_compatibility_form(&self, schema: &Value) -> bool; }` (crates/vtest-adapter-api/src/lib.rs:438-441), with `AdapterCapability::StructuredTest`, `AdapterRegistration.structured_test`, `AdapterRegistry::structured_test(id)` and `missing_capability_semantics(StructuredTest) = OperationRejected` (lib.rs:223, 469, 596-604, 646). chain.condition: A `.verify/forms/<kind>.yaml` whose top-level `adapter` field is absent and whose `kind` is claimed by no adapter (e.g. `pytest-case`), driven through `vtest test create --form pytest-case --answers …`. Match count is necessarily 0 — not merely 'no matcher accepted', but no crate registers a StructuredTestAdapter at all (grep for `StructuredTestAdapter|structured_test|AdapterCapability::StructuredTest` across vtest-adapter-rust/, vtest-scan/, vtest-cli/ returns nothing). chain.expected: `vtest test create --form pytest-case` rejects the operation (owner absent, 0 matches) and leaves src/lib.rs unchanged; no rust-cargo Test is produced from an unowned Form.

chain.claim: For each REQ §11 violation class there is a designated deterministic rule among DA-001..DA-006 such that any Test exhibiting that class within the rule's deterministic scope receives non-PASS on that rule, AND a Test exhibiting no class receives no FAIL from any rule — for arbitrary inputs, independent of any fixture corpus. Note the asymmetry: 'within the rule's deterministic scope' qualifies only the positive conjunct; the no-false-FAIL conjunct is unqualified, so analysis scope never excuses a FAIL (that is what UNKNOWN is for).
chain.normative_source:
All four VO refs re-read in full.
(1) 要件定義 §11 (要件定義・要件分解 v0.1.md:477-509) enumerates the violation classes: constant assertion (assert!(true)), declared Source Target not executed, target called but result unverified, self-comparison, and the catch-all 'その他、同様に検証結果が対象実装の正しさに依存しない構造' (l.507) — a SEMANTIC criterion (does the verification outcome depend on the target implementation's correctness?), not a syntactic one. l.509: '決定論的解析で明確にNGとできるTestは、LLM監査へ送る前に拒否可能であること' — pre-LLM rejection is authorized only for tests that are CLEARLY NG.
(2) 基本仕様 §7.2 (基本仕様 v0.1.md:359-377) lists what rust-cargo must at least detect: constant-only assertion / unconfirmed target call / result unverified / self-comparison / empty body. 'no verification syntax at all' (DA-006) is NOT in that list. l.370-371: '判定は保守的に行う。決定論的に確定できる違反のみ FAIL とし、確定できないものは UNKNOWN として意味監査へ送る。' l.372: FAIL ⇒ may be rejected before semantic audit.
(3) 別紙C §18.3.2 (別紙C 受入仕様 v0.1.md:91-95): 'DA-001〜DA-006とW-DA-101は本冊 §7の判定条件に従う' / '確定違反だけをFAILとし、解析限界をUNKNOWNとして保持する' / '正常Testは違反なしとなり…' — the second conjunct stated verbatim at the acceptance layer.
(4) 詳細設計 §7.1-§7.2 (詳細設計 v0.1.md:955-996). §7.1 l.960-961: '決定論的に確定できる違反のみ FAIL とする。解析の限界で確定できない場合は FAIL ではなく UNKNOWN とし、意味監査へ委ねる。' §7.2 l.971-976 defines 'assert相当の構文' as a CLOSED syntactic list (assert!/assert_eq!/assert_ne!/panic! + config assertion_macros; #[should_panic]; .unwrap()/.expect()/?; Result-returning fn that can Err) — a call to a same-file assert helper is not in it. l.985 table row: 'DA-006 検証構文なし | 関数内に assert 相当が1つも存在しない | FAIL条件: 該当 | UNKNOWNへ退避する例: なし'. l.996: DA-001..DA-006 FAIL ⇒ excluded from the semantic-audit bundle by default.
chain.mechanism: DA-006 is the rule realizing REQ §11's catch-all class ('structures whose verification outcome does not depend on the target implementation's correctness'). Its designed detection proxy is purely syntactic and function-body-local: 'the function contains no assert-equivalent syntax', with the assert-equivalent set closed to macros/attributes/unwrap/expect/?/Result-Err. The design deliberately grants NO UNKNOWN escape to DA-006 (§7.2 l.985 '退避例: なし'), even though the same document grants such escapes to DA-002 (which explicitly explores 同一ファイル内の呼出先 helper 1段) and DA-003 (§7.2 l.981-982, l.988), and even though §7.1 / 基本仕様 §7.2 / 別紙C §18.3.2 all mandate UNKNOWN — not FAIL — whenever a violation cannot be deterministically confirmed. Delegating the assertion to a helper function moves the assert-equivalent syntax one call-frame out of the analyzed body; DA-006's body-local proxy then reads 'no verification at all' and emits a confirmed FAIL.
chain.condition: A Test that (a) calls its declared Source Target, (b) binds the result, and (c) verifies that result by passing it to an assert helper function (assertion inside the helper, not inside the test body), and contains no inline assert!/assert_eq!/panic!/unwrap()/expect()/?, no #[should_panic], and does not return Result. Not an exotic input — it is the dominant idiom of this repository's own CLI acceptance suite (TEST-CLI-022/023/060 delegate to assert_adapter_usage_error / assert_ok / assert_tree_child; crates/vtest-cli/tests/adapter_acceptance.rs:761, m2_acceptance.rs:111, m2_acceptance.rs:182).
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-adapter-rust/src/static_audit.rs:1190 has_assert_like(item: &ItemFn, assertion_macros) — collect_assertions (l.1296) + VerificationSyntaxVisitor (l.1201+) + returns_result_and_can_err, all visiting ONLY the test's own ItemFn; no callee/helper expansion (contrast rule_da002, which does perform same-file 1-level helper exploration). Result consumed at static_audit.rs:1777 (let has_assert = has_assert_like(...)) and turned into the DA-006 RuleResult at static_audit.rs:1800-1812: verdict = if has_assert { Pass } else { Fail } — Fail is the only non-Pass branch, so UNKNOWN is unreachable for DA-006. is_assertion_macro (l.1326) matches syn::Macro nodes only, so the assertion_macros config cannot whitelist a helper *function* — no config escape hatch. FAIL then flows to the persisted Audit Record verdict and to the bundle gate (vtest audit bundle default skip on static FAIL).
chain.expected: Per the claim (and 別紙C §18.3.2 '正常Testは違反なしとなり', 基本仕様 §7.2 l.370-371, 詳細設計 §7.1 l.960-961): this Test exhibits none of REQ §11's classes — the target IS called, the result IS verified, no constant assertion, no self-comparison, body non-empty, and its verification outcome DOES depend on the target implementation's correctness. Therefore no rule may return FAIL. The correct verdict for a body-local analyzer that cannot see into the helper is UNKNOWN (analysis limit), leaving the Test to semantic audit.
chain.actual: Reproduced on the prebuilt binary in an isolated project: DA-006 = FAIL, reason 'no assert-like syntax is present'; record verdict = FAIL, with DA-006 the SOLE FAIL (DA-001 PASS, DA-002 UNKNOWN, DA-003 UNKNOWN, DA-004 PASS, DA-005 PASS). The control Test with an inline assert_eq! over the same target gets DA-006 = PASS and record verdict = UNKNOWN. Downstream, `vtest audit bundle --kind test-semantic --test TEST-HELPER-ASSERT` returns {"skipped":true,"reason":"static audit verdict is FAIL; pass --include-failed to force a bundle"} while the control Test is bundled normally. Mutating the target (a+b → a-b) makes the helper-delegating Test FAIL under cargo test, empirically proving its verification outcome depends on the implementation's correctness — i.e. it is not in REQ §11's catch-all class.
chain.negation:
The second conjunct is negated at SYSTEM level, not merely locally.
(1) Reachability: `vtest scan` accepts the Test with zero diagnostics (files 2 / sources 4 / tests 2), so no earlier gate rejects it; and the shape is the prevailing idiom in the tool's own suite.
(2) No other gate rejects first and the FAIL is not redundant: DA-006 is the only FAIL on the record; every other rule is PASS or UNKNOWN. Absent the DA-006 defect the record verdict would be UNKNOWN, not FAIL.
(3) The consequence discriminates. I deliberately do NOT rest on the verify-time static_audit item: the control Test also shows static_audit FAIL there (DA-002 UNKNOWN with no runtime proof, §7.3 未充足), so that observation does not separate the cases. The clean discriminators are (a) the persisted canonical Audit Record verdict FAIL vs UNKNOWN, and (b) `audit bundle` default exclusion — the helper-delegating Test is REJECTED BEFORE SEMANTIC AUDIT while the control Test is bundled. That pre-LLM rejection is exactly the operation REQ §11 l.509 authorizes only for Tests that 決定論的解析で明確にNGとできる. A Test that verifiably depends on the implementation is therefore barred from both the deterministic PASS path and the LLM audit path, with no route to rehabilitation.
(4) No escape hatch: assertion_macros matches syn::Macro nodes only; a helper is an ExprCall, so no configuration can make this PASS or UNKNOWN.
(5) Scope defence fails: the claim qualifies only the positive conjunct with 'within the rule's deterministic scope'. Analysis scope can excuse a missed detection, never a false FAIL — 詳細設計 §7.1, 基本仕様 §7.2 l.370-371 and 別紙C §18.3.2 all mandate UNKNOWN for exactly this out-of-scope situation.
(6) Not a spec gap. The implementation faithfully implements the 詳細設計 §7.2 DA-006 row ('UNKNOWNへ退避する例: なし'), so the defect is that row itself, which contradicts REQ §11 + 基本仕様 §7.2 + 別紙C §18.3.2 + its own §7.1 conservatism principle. The competing 'structural' reading of REQ §11's catch-all (treat 'no verification syntax in the body' as itself a class) does not stand on the spec's own text: the catch-all is worded semantically (検証結果が対象実装の正しさに依存しない構造) and I empirically falsified its antecedent by mutation; moreover the design already treats the identical analysis limit as UNKNOWN for DA-002/DA-003 and even performs 1-level same-file helper exploration for DA-002. Fix direction is spec-side (give DA-006 an UNKNOWN escape, or extend assert-equivalence to helper delegation), but the VO claim as written is broken in running behavior.

chain.claim: VO-PLAN-05: 'A spec-coverage submission is accepted only when its reasons include the adopted requirements, the corresponding REQs, and the excluded passages with grounds (別紙C §18.3.4); otherwise it is rejected and spec_coverage stays non-PASS.'

chain.mechanism: Designed mechanism: (a) `vtest audit bundle --kind spec-coverage` emits a bundle bound to the SPEC subject content hash and the complete set of active REQs referencing it; (b) an agent/human submits an Audit Record whose reasons must carry 取り込み要求事項 / 対応REQ / exclusion根拠, otherwise submission is rejected (empty reasons, schema violation, kind mismatch, stale bundle hash → reject, 別紙C:144); (c) verify evaluates spec_coverage at the SPEC evaluation point by consuming only a *valid, non-stale, COMPLETE* spec-coverage Audit Record — absence of any audit maps to NOT_CHECKED, never PASS.
chain.condition: A project with a registered current SPEC source, one active REQ whose spec_refs point at that SPEC, and one VO listing that REQ in `requirements` — and zero spec-coverage Audit Records (necessarily zero, since the kind cannot be bundled or stored). It never opens an Audit Record, never reads the SPEC record, never checks source currency or hash. chain.mechanism: Design mechanism: two independent audit kinds and two independent check items. `spec-coverage` audit binds a SPEC subject to its complete corresponding active-REQ set and yields COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE/UNKNOWN, feeding the `spec_coverage` item evaluated at the SPEC node. `vo-coverage` audit binds an active REQ to its VO set, feeding the `vo_coverage` item at REQ/VO nodes. Each verdict is stored as its own Audit record and drives only its own item.
chain.condition: A project where (a) every active REQ happens to have at least one linked VO, and (b) Spec->REQ intake is demonstrably incomplete - either no Specification is registered at all (別紙C L158 => MISSING) or a Specification is registered whose requirements are captured by no REQ and that no active REQ references (詳細設計 L1346 => MISSING), and (c) no spec-coverage audit exists (=> NOT_CHECKED per 詳細設計 L1346). Then observe the stored `spec_coverage` result.

chain.claim: An active REQ declares one or more spec_refs: (a) `vtest req add/edit` rejects an active REQ without a --spec/--section pair, (b) a stored active REQ lacking spec_refs is schema-invalid so spec_coverage yields MISMATCH and never PASS, and (c) a withdrawn REQ retains its refs but is excluded from spec_coverage's current corresponding-REQ set.
chain.normative_source: VERIFIED verbatim in three layers. (1) 詳細設計 v0.1 §3.2 (docs/AI並列開発向けテスト検証システム 詳細設計 v0.1.md:234-235): 「active REQは1件以上の`spec_refs`を必須とする。`withdrawn` REQは履歴表示のため参照を保持するが、`spec_coverage`の現在の対応REQ集合には含めない。」 (2) 詳細設計 §11.1 spec_coverage 判定 (same file:1350): 「対象SPECを参照するactive REQが0件なら`MISSING`。REQの`spec_refs.spec`が解決不能、`section`が空、またはschema不正なら`MISMATCH`」, and :1353 「REQ / VO / TEST scopeは対象SPECの対応active REQ集合を埋めない」. (3) 別紙A インターフェース仕様, `vtest req add / edit` section: the usage grammar lists `--spec SPEC-X --section <sec>` UNBRACKETED (mandatory) while --parent/--status are bracketed, and states 「active REQは1件以上の`--spec` / `--section`組を必須とする。withdrawn REQは既存参照を保持できる。」 (4) 別紙C 受入仕様:81 restates it as an acceptance criterion. All three facets are explicit normative text, not inference.
chain.mechanism: The Specification→REQ edge is the root of the traceability graph. The canonical writer (vtest req add/edit) is the gate that refuses to persist an active REQ with no Specification anchor; the reader-side gate (scan E-SCAN-012 plus verify's spec_coverage, evaluated at the SPEC point) is the fail-closed backstop mapping a schema-invalid or unanchored REQ to MISMATCH. `status: withdrawn` is the designed escape valve: it preserves history without polluting the current corresponding-REQ set.
chain.condition: A project where an operator runs `vtest req add --id REQ-NOSPEC --summary "..."` with no --spec/--section, links a VO to it, and runs verify; plus a second REQ set to `status: withdrawn` present during a full verify.
chain.impl_path: crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:2792-2831 add_req (validates id/summary/parent only; `spec_refs = spec_refs_from_args(...)`, then hardcodes `status: "active"`); crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:3646-3670 spec_refs_from_args (an empty `specs` slice maps to an empty Vec with no error; also defaults `section` to "" when --section is omitted); crates/vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:2934+ edit_req (same path, status settable to active with no refs check); crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:735-766 validate_req_record (missing_fields checks only id/summary/status/created/updated, then only that status is active|withdrawn — spec_refs emptiness is never examined; E-SCAN-012 does not exist anywhere in crates/, scan defines only E-SCAN-001..011); crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:546-585 evaluate_item("spec_coverage") (reads selection.req_ids and vo records, tests only whether some vo.requirements contains req.id; returns Pass or Missing — spec_refs is never read, MISMATCH is not in this branch's value domain, and no status filter is applied); crates/vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:164-246 ScopeSelection (req_ids = all REQ record keys for a full verify, with no active/withdrawn partition).
chain.expected: (a) `req add` without --spec exits non-zero with E-OP-001 and writes no record. (b) With a refs-less active REQ stored, spec_coverage = MISMATCH (schema-invalid REQ), never PASS. (c) In a full verify, a withdrawn REQ is not a member of the corresponding-REQ set, so spec_coverage neither PASSes nor fails on account of it.
chain.actual: (a) `req add --id REQ-NOSPEC --summary "no spec refs at all"` exits 0 and writes `spec_refs: []` with `status: 'active'`. (b) `verify --req REQ-NOSPEC` reports spec_coverage = PASS, basis "every selected REQ has at least one linked VO" — the refs-less state is invisible to the check. (c) Full `verify` reports spec_coverage = MISSING with basis "selected REQ record(s) have no linked VO: REQ-WD", where REQ-WD has `status: 'withdrawn'` — the withdrawn REQ is inside the corresponding-REQ set and actively degrades the verdict. `scan` emits no error diagnostic at all for the refs-less active REQ (only an unrelated W-SCAN-102 warning about VO isolation).
chain.negation: Decisive at SYSTEM level, and each facet is independently sufficient. (1) Reachability: the state is produced by the product's own supported command with valid arguments — no file hand-editing, no legacy reader path. (2) No other gate rejects first: every downstream gate on the path was checked. scan's validate_req_record never inspects spec_refs and emits nothing; E-SCAN-012, the diagnostic 詳細設計:849 assigns to exactly this class, is entirely unimplemented (zero occurrences in crates/), so the reader-side backstop does not exist; vo_decomposition — which §11.1.1 says must go MISSING/MISMATCH on unresolvable or empty spec_refs, and which §11.1.1 explicitly binds to E-SCAN-012 — returned PASS with basis "scan and canonical VO records are structurally readable". The overall verify result was MISSING, but solely from test_existence (no covering Test), an orthogonal item; spec_coverage's own emitted value is PASS, and §4.3 priority folding cannot turn a PASS item into MISMATCH. The claim's operative predicate — spec_coverage MISMATCH, never PASS — is therefore directly negated by an emitted PASS. (3) Facet (c) negates in the opposite direction: exclusion is not merely unimplemented, the withdrawn REQ is affirmatively counted, so the spec's history-preservation escape valve is inoperative — withdrawing a REQ cannot clear the current set. (4) The contradiction is frozen green by the suite, so it is not a transient omission: TEST-CLI-060 (crates/vtest-cli/tests/m2_acceptance.rs:589-606) asserts `req add --id REQ-M2-TREE-ROOT --summary "root requirement"` with no --spec is OK, and TEST-CLI-093 (crates/vtest-cli/tests/m9_acceptance.rs:800-810) asserts `req_upsert` of REQ-M9-OTHER with no specs/sections is OK — the suite asserts exactly what the spec forbids. One secondary defect beyond the candidate's citation: spec_refs_from_args (lib.rs:3665) defaults `section` to "" when --spec is given without --section, minting the empty-section state that 詳細設計:849/:1350 designate E-SCAN-012/MISMATCH. The candidate's code-reading was accurate and if anything understated.

chain.normative_source: VERIFIED against the docs themselves. Kihon-shiyou (basic spec) 7.4, docs/AI...基本仕様 v0.1.md around lines 429-437: 'the judgment result MUST carry the following structured reasons' listing (1) the spec location relied on (SPEC ID + section reference), (2) the decomposition viewpoint (which axis/partition), (3) the conditions excluded and the spec location grounding that exclusion, (4) examples as needed.
